guide.summary: A fungus whose threads pass food along to hungry parts and that turns starch into sugar.
guide.biology: Some real fungal networks move water and nutrients through their threads, from well-fed parts to parts that need them.
guide.rules: Stays attached to gel, sediment, mesh or beads and never swims. Eats sugar first, then detritus, using oxygen. When starch is in or beside its cell and it has more than 35 energy, it releases starch enzyme at 0.40 energy per second; the sugar that enzyme makes is free for anyone nearby. Each new segment grows into a free neighboring cell with the most usable food, and a daughter that shares a side with its parent is joined to it by a transport link, up to 4 links per segment. A segment above its starting body sends up to 0.02 carbon per second along each link to a linked segment below 1.5 times its starting body, never more than half the difference; energy is never shared. Comfortable at pH 4.5 to 7, warmth 0.30 to 0.65 and salinity up to 0.25. Fungal inhibitor affects it. Waterbears graze single segments, and Threadrider can attach to active segments.
guide.example: Grow a Cordweaver line from a sugar patch out across bare gel and watch food travel along it to the far tips.
